reports.title: BC Assessment Authority (property assessment roll and related products)
reports.description: Provincial Crown corporation established under the Assessment Authority Act and Assessment Act that produces the annual uniform province-wide assessment roll for more than two million properties, valuing most at market value as of 1 July of the preceding year; supplies the completed, revised and supplementary rolls (and Data Advice extracts) to municipalities, regional districts and provincial taxing authorities as the sole base for property-value taxation.
reports.cadence_note: annual (roll completed by 31 December; notices mailed early January; revised roll after Property Assessment Review Panel; weekly/monthly Data Advice updates)

reports.title: Assessment Roll Quality (Assessment-to-Sales Ratio and Coefficient of Dispersion metrics)
reports.description: Annual public reporting of median Assessment-to-Sales Ratio (ASR) and Coefficient of Dispersion (COD) for residential, strata-residential and non-residential properties against International Association of Assessing Officers (IAAO) standards, demonstrating accuracy and uniformity of the assessment roll.

reports.title: Year-End Assessment Roll Report
reports.description: Report supplied to taxing authorities covering assessment trends, risk-to-roll, roll stability, market-movement summaries (July 1 values), assessment initiatives, information-exchange requirements and legislative/case-law updates to support municipal financial planning and appeal-reserve allocation.

reports.title: BC Assessment Annual Service Plan Report
reports.description: Statutory annual report under the Budget Transparency and Accountability Act comparing actual results against the three-year service plan, including assessment-roll quality metrics, financial statements and performance against mandate to produce uniform assessments.

reports.title: Budget and Fiscal Plan (British Columbia)
reports.description: Principal annual budget document presenting the three-year fiscal plan (revenues, expenses, capital, debt), economic review and outlook, major assumptions and risks, tax measures and federal-transfer projections; tabled with the Estimates and accompanying ministry/Crown service plans.

reports.title: City of Vancouver Annual Financial Report
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements and accompanying management discussion prepared in accordance with Public Sector Accounting Standards, reporting financial position, results of operations, cash flows and accumulated surplus for the City of Vancouver.

reports.title: City of Vancouver Operating and Capital Budget / Five-Year Financial Plan
reports.description: Annual operating budget and multi-year capital plan setting expenditure authorities, property-tax levy, utility rates and service levels; approved by Council and used as the baseline for subsequent quarterly reviews and the following year's tax-rating bylaws.

reports.title: City of Vancouver Tax Rating Bylaws (General Purpose Tax and related)
reports.description: Annual bylaws establishing municipal general-purpose tax rates (and rates for Metro Vancouver Regional District, Municipal Finance Authority and other authorities after land-assessment averaging) applied to the BC Assessment taxable values for each property class; enacted after budget approval and before the statutory May deadline.

reports.title: City of Victoria Financial Plan (multi-year)
reports.description: Five-year financial plan adopted by Council under the Community Charter, setting operating and capital expenditures, property-tax revenue requirements and tax-distribution policy for the City of Victoria.

reports.title: City of Victoria Annual Report (audited financial statements) and Statement of Financial Information
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Public Sector Accounting Standards together with the Statement of Financial Information required by the Financial Information Act, reporting revenues (including taxation), expenses, financial position and accumulated surplus.

reports.title: BC Housing Rental Assistance Program (RAP) and related frameworks
reports.description: Provincial portable rental-assistance program providing monthly benefits to eligible low-income families (and parallel SAFER for seniors) calculated from an income/rent-gap formula subject to province-wide maximum rent ceilings; administered by BC Housing under published program frameworks.
reports.cadence_note: ongoing (framework updated periodically; benefit parameters reviewed annually)

reports.title: Public Accounts of the Province of British Columbia (Consolidated Summary Financial Statements)
reports.publisher: Office of the Comptroller General, Ministry of Finance
reports.description: Annual audited consolidated Summary Financial Statements of the government reporting entity (ministries, Crown corporations, school districts, universities, colleges, institutes and health organizations) together with Financial Statement Discussion and Analysis, Consolidated Revenue Fund extracts and detailed schedules; compares actual results to the prior Budget and Fiscal Plan.
reports.cadence_note: annual (typically July–August for the fiscal year ended 31 March)

reports.title: Local Government Data Entry (LGDE) forms and Local Government Statistics
reports.publisher: Ministry of Housing and Municipal Affairs
reports.description: Standardized annual financial and statistical return required of every local government (due 15 May) presenting assets, liabilities, revenues, expenditures and other indicators drawn from audited financial statements; the Ministry reviews submissions and publishes aggregate Local Government Statistics. Also collects current-year tax rates. Functional counterpart to Alberta’s FIR + Municipal Financial and Statistical Data compilation.
reports.cadence_note: annual (submission deadline 15 May; statistics published thereafter)

reports.title: Metro Vancouver Regional District Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements of the Metro Vancouver Regional District, Greater Vancouver Water District, Greater Vancouver Sewerage and Drainage District and Metro Vancouver Housing Corporation, prepared under Public Sector Accounting Standards.

reports.title: Metro Vancouver Financial Plan / Budget
reports.description: Multi-year financial plan and annual operating/capital budget for Metro Vancouver’s regional services (water, liquid waste, solid waste, regional parks, air quality, housing, etc.), funded in part by requisitions collected through municipal property-tax bills.

reports.title: BC Stats Population Estimates (sub-provincial)
reports.description: Annual (and quarterly highlight) population estimates for municipalities, regional districts, development regions and other sub-provincial geographies, produced by BC Stats and kept consistent in aggregate with Statistics Canada provincial totals.

reports.title: 2026 Residential School Tax Rates Order (OIC 124/26)
reports.publisher: Province of British Columbia (Lieutenant Governor in Council)
reports.description: Annual Order in Council under section 119(3) of the School Act setting the residential (Class 1) school tax rate, expressed in dollars per thousand dollars of net taxable value, for each school district in British Columbia for the calendar year.

reports.title: 2026 Non-Residential School Tax Rates Order (OIC 122/26)
reports.publisher: Province of British Columbia (Lieutenant Governor in Council)
reports.description: Annual Order in Council under section 119(3) of the School Act setting the school tax rates for all non-residential property classes (Utilities, Supportive Housing, Major Industry, Light Industry, Business and Other, Managed Forest Land, Recreational/Non-Profit, Farm) province-wide for the calendar year.

reports.title: Additional School Tax rate (high-value residential properties)
reports.publisher: Province of British Columbia, Ministry of Finance / Ministry of Education and Child Care
reports.description: Provincial surtax applied to the residential portion of properties assessed above $3 million (0.2 % between $3–4 million and 0.4 % above $4 million; rates scheduled to rise in 2027). BC Assessment determines applicability; the tax is collected with the regular school tax on the municipal or Surveyor of Taxes notice.

reports.title: South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority 2026 Property Tax Bylaw (No. 163-2026) and Replacement Tax Bylaw (No. 164-2026)
reports.publisher: South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority (TransLink)
reports.description: Annual bylaws setting the property-tax and fixed replacement-tax rates levied by TransLink on the net taxable value of land and improvements in the transportation service region; rates are applied by member municipalities on the BC Assessment roll and form part of the property-tax bill.

reports.title: School District No. 39 (Vancouver) Annual Budget and Amended Annual Budget
reports.publisher: Board of Education of School District No. 39 (Vancouver)
reports.description: Annual (and mid-year amended) budget bylaw under the School Act setting estimated revenues, expenses and total budget bylaw amount for the Vancouver public school district, including Ministry operating grants, tuition, and other revenue sources.

reports.title: School District No. 39 (Vancouver) Audited Financial Statements and Statement of Financial Information (SOFI)
reports.publisher: Board of Education of School District No. 39 (Vancouver)
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under the accounting requirements of the Budget Transparency and Accountability Act and accompanying Statement of Financial Information required by the Financial Information Act, covering the Vancouver public school district.

reports.title: School District No. 93 (Conseil scolaire francophone) Annual Budget and Amended Budget
reports.publisher: Conseil scolaire francophone de la Colombie-Britannique
reports.description: Annual and amended budgets for the province-wide francophone public school district (SD 93), prepared under the School Act and reporting Ministry operating grants, other revenues and expenses for French-language education.

reports.title: School District No. 93 (Conseil scolaire francophone) Audited Financial Statements, SOFI and Financial Statement Discussion & Analysis
reports.publisher: Conseil scolaire francophone de la Colombie-Britannique
reports.description: Audited financial statements, Statement of Financial Information and management discussion for the francophone school district, prepared under the Budget Transparency and Accountability Act accounting requirements.

reports.title: Funding Rates for Independent Schools (Group 1 and Group 2 per-FTE rates)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Education and Child Care, Independent Schools Branch
reports.description: Annual table of estimated per-FTE student funding rates for Group 1 (50 % of local public district rate) and Group 2 (35 % of local public district rate) independent schools, published by school district for use in calculating operating grants.

reports.title: Grants to Independent Schools policy
reports.publisher: Ministry of Education and Child Care
reports.description: Official policy describing the operating-grant framework for Group 1 and Group 2 independent schools, including eligibility, percentage rates relative to the local public district, payment schedule and audit requirements.

dependencies.basis: The ASR and COD metrics are calculated directly from the assessment roll values produced by BC Assessment and the corresponding sale prices of properties that sold near the July 1 valuation date. The document states: "An Assessment to Sales Ratio (ASR) is calculated by dividing the property’s assessed value by the property’s selling price. ... For the 2026 Assessment Roll, BC Assessment’s median ASR for single-family residential properties, strata residential properties ... and non-residential are within the targeted range."

Municipal tax rates are applied to the taxable assessed values supplied by BC Assessment; the Community Charter defines assessed value as the value determined under the Assessment Act, and Vancouver's rating bylaws and tax notices explicitly use the BC Assessment roll as the tax base. The document states: ""assessed value" means assessed value determined under the Assessment Act; "assessment roll" means an assessment roll within the meaning of the Assessment Act"

The annual tax-rating bylaws are enacted after Council approval of the operating budget and set the rates required to raise the property-tax levy authorized in that budget (subject to land-assessment averaging). The document states: "On November 25, 2025, Council approved the 2026 Operating Budget based on a Council-directed property tax increase of 0%. ... 2026 Rating By-law – General Purpose Tax ... that establishes the 2026 municipal general purpose tax rates"

The City of Victoria's audited consolidated financial statements are prepared in compliance with the Community Charter and Public Sector Accounting Board standards. The document states: "The financial statements are the responsibility of the City of Victoria’s management and have been prepared in compliance with Section 167 of the Community Charter and in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles approved by the Public Sector Accounting Board."

Property-tax revenue requirements in the Financial Plan are calculated from the taxable assessed values supplied by BC Assessment; tax rates are set on that base after the plan is adopted. The document states: "In 2026, the increase in revenue needed from property taxes is $14.185 million over 2025, resulting in an overall tax increase of 7.28 per cent ... This will result in an average property tax increase of $323 for an average residential property assessed at $1,015,000"

The fiscal plan's revenue forecast explicitly incorporates the Canada Health Transfer (and related health agreements) as a major federal contribution, with growth assumptions tied to national nominal GDP. The document states: "Federal transfers include $2.2 billion over three years in targeted federal funding for health services (e.g., $447 million under Aging with Dignity agreement, $653 million for expanded public coverage for diabetes and hormone replacement therapy, $1.1 billion for extension of Working Together to Improve Health Care for Canadians agreement, in addition to Canada Health Transfer)."

The Annual Service Plan Report is the statutory accountability document for the BC Assessment Authority itself, reporting performance against the mandate to produce the uniform assessment roll. The document states: "BC Assessment is a provincial Crown corporation with the legislated mandate to establish and maintain property assessments that are uniform in the whole of British Columbia, in accordance with the Assessment Act. While BC Assessment has no direct role in property taxation, it plays an integral and impartial role in the provincial property taxation system by producing an accurate and uniform assessment roll each year for over two million properties in the province."
